title: How a Welding Torch Works in 60 Seconds 🔥⚙️ #shorts
description:
An oxy-acetylene torch burns at about 3,500°C, hot enough to melt steel. Oxygen and acetylene flow from two tanks, mix inside the torch, and burn at the tip in a sharp blue cone. The heat melts metal edges into a puddle that fuses as it cools. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#welding #metalwork #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: This flame burns at about *3,500 degrees* Celsius, hot enough to melt steel.

steps.label: Tanks
steps.text: Two tanks feed the torch: *oxygen* and *acetylene* fuel, each through its own regulator and hose.

steps.label: Mixing
steps.text: Two valves on the handle set each flow, and the gases blend in a *mixing chamber*.

steps.label: Flame
steps.text: Lit at the tip, a balanced flame shows a sharp *inner cone*. The hottest spot is just past its tip.

steps.label: Weld
steps.text: That heat melts both metal edges into a *molten puddle*, and a *filler rod* adds extra metal.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.text: As the puddle *cools*, the two pieces freeze into one solid joint.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Mix, ignite, *melt*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
